newsitem.title: USA: Edsel Ford II to change jobs at automaker - report.
newsitem.headline: Edsel Ford II to change jobs at automaker - report.

text.p: Edsel Ford II will leave his job as president and chief operating officer of Ford Motor Co.'s Ford Credit unit and become vice president of customer satisfaction, the Detroit News reported Tuesday.
The move is expected to be announced in October, the paper said. Ford spokeswoman Pam Kueber would not comment, adding, "We're not going to contribute to speculation."
Edsel Ford II, 48 years old, is the great grandson of company founder Henry Ford, and the son of Henry Ford II, who ran the company from 1945-1980.

He is one of three Ford family members who sit on the automaker's board of directors, and the only one to work in senior management ranks. The Ford family controls 40 percent of the firm's voting stock.
Edsel Ford has worked at Ford Motor Co. since 1974, holding a variety of sales and marketing positions before being named president of Ford Credit in 1991.

The News, citing unnamed sources, said Ford will return to the automotive side of the business by taking over the customer satisfaction position from Thomas Wagner, who is expected to retire at the end of this year.
Ford Credit is the largest unit within Ford's Financial Services Group, providing financing for a variety of Ford customers, and offering various insurance and other financial service products.

Edsel Ford has presided over a time of strong profits, international expansion and at Ford Credit. However, higher credit losses and lower margins from increasing depreciation expenses on leased vehicles have reduced the unit's earnings this year.
Ford's stock fell 37.5 cents to $40.31 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.
